results.title: AI, affair and espionage: Why is Nvidia's chief Jensen Huang under scrutiny?
results.content: Nvidia chief and tech titan Jensen Huang was in the spotlight on Monday after acknowledging an affair with a woman US officials say was working for Chinese intelligence, a claim Beijing denied.

results.title: 'A tricky day' ahead for French PM as he meets with unions amid social unrest
results.content: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is to meet unions and employer federation representatives on Monday to discuss salaries and purchasing power following a wave of social unrest across France in recent weeks. But, says France 24's Rochelle Ferguson, he faces a tricky task if his is to meet unions' wage demands and take steps towards placating widespread public anger.

results.title: French policemen go on trial over 2020 beating of Black music producer
results.content: Three French policemen went on trial on Monday, November 9, over the beating of a Black music producer they say was not wearing a face mask during the Covid pandemic, in a rare police brutality case to go to court. The assault on Michel Zecler, now 47, triggered renewed outrage in France over police violence, which victims and researchers say is systemic.

results.title: 'Novaya Gazeta', an independent Russian newspaper critical of Putin, closes
results.content: Russian investigative newspaper Novaya ⁠Gazeta was winding ​up its operations on Monday, November 9, and preparing to quit its central Moscow office after holding its ​final editorial meeting, bowing to what it said was a campaign of state pressure that had made it impossible to carry on reporting.

results.title: COP31 opens with leaders under pressure to tackle climate crisis
results.content: The COP31 climate talks kicked off Monday, November 9, with an early fight over money as the UN's chief urged world leaders to "get serious" about tackling the crisis after a year of devastating weather extremes. Antonio Guterres made his plea as thousands of participants descended on a sprawling expo centre in the Turkish Mediterranean city of Antalya for the UN's annual two-week climate conference.

results.title: New James Bond actor expected 'within weeks' as 'unexpected' frontrunners emerge
results.content: PRESS REVIEW – Monday, November 9: Papers condemn the Kremlin's closure of Russian independent paper Novaya Gazeta on its last day. Also in Russia: leaked numbers suggest that almost half a million Russians have died in the war in Ukraine. Next: NASA is recruiting astronauts who will live and work on the Moon. Finally: who will be the next James Bond?

results.title: Tents 'entirely submerged' has heavy rains hit Gaza
results.content: More than three years after the start of the war in Gaza, Palestinians displaced by the conflict are still left out in the cold. This week, torrential rain has been soaking makeshift camps, leaving many people without shelter as winter approaches.

results.title: The white truffles sparking bidding frenzies in northern Italy
results.content: In northern Italy, the white truffle capital of the world, the small round fungi are selling at auction for tens of thousands of euros. And as the climate changes, truffles are becoming increasingly rare, with less supply and ever more demand pushing up prices even further.

results.title: 🔴 Judo star Teddy Riner announces bid for French presidency
Judo star Teddy Riner announces bid for French presidency
results.content: French judo star Teddy Riner announced on Monday that he would run in next year's high-stakes presidential election, pledging to be a "president who brings people together".

results.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts Houthi missiles as Riyadh's Aramco building damaged
results.content: Saudi Arabia intercepted incoming missiles from Yemen's Houthi rebels targeting the kingdom's capital and other regions on Sunday, November 8, with falling debris damaging a building belonging to the state-owned oil giant Aramco in Riyadh’s financial district.

results.title: French PM Lecornu holds talks over protesters' cost-of-living concerns
results.content: French Prime ⁠Minister Sebastien Lecornu is set to meet ​representatives of employers' organisations and private-sector unions on Monday, November 9, to try ​to address cost-of-living concerns that have sparked some of France's worst civil unrest in years.

results.title: Poland begins 2 days of national mourning after gunman kills 6
results.content: Poland has begun two days of national mourning after a gunman opened fire in Krakow's main square Saturday afternoon, November 7. Six people were killed and at least 15 were injured. The gunman was shot and detained by police. He then died later in hospital.

results.title: Israel's opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has six weeks to form a government
results.content: Israeli President Isaac Herzog formally gave opposition politician Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form the next government Sunday evening, leaving Eisenkot six weeks to try to put together a coalition to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. FRANCE 24's correspondent in Jerusalem Noga Tarnopolsky has more.

results.title: Nvidia probe 'to impact the whole of the world'
results.content: In this week's Asia View, France 24's correspondent Jan Camezind Broomby takes a look at the announcement by chip giant Nvidia that it has opened a probe into chief executive and co-founder Jensen Huang after he acknowledged an affair with a woman US officials say was working for Chinese intelligence. It is a development that, Camezind Broomby, says, could have a far-reaching impact not just in Asia but across the world.

results.title: Dems set to go after Hegseth, Musk following midterms rout
results.content: House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries has indicated he and his fellow Democrats would back an impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, citing his role in the unpopular Iran war launched by Donald Trump in February. Tech megabillionaire Elon Musk will also likely be the target of a congressional probe when Democrats take control of Congress in January following their comprehensive victory in the midterms, senior lawmakers said on Sunday.

results.title: Paris police officers go on trial over 2020 beating of Black man
results.content: Three French police officers will go on trial Monday over the 2020 beating of Black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris. The assault, which was captured on camera, sparked nationwide outrage and renewed scrutiny of police violence and racism in France.

results.title: European troops in Poland: 'Coalition of the Willing' holds military exercises
results.content: Some 2,800 troops from 10 different European countries are taking part in a multinational military exercise in Poland. The aim is to prepare European forces for a possible deployment to Ukraine after hostilities end.

results.title: French PM holds 'social conference': just 'an exercise in PR'?
results.content: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is to meet unions and employer federation representatives on Monday to discuss salaries and purchasing power, with a possible raise to the minimum wage on the cards. It comes amid a wave of social unrest across France in recent weeks that has seen strikes sometimes violent protests. But, with the government constrained by an ongoing budget crisis, the meeting feels “more like something of an exercise in PR”, says France 24 reporter Luke Shrago.

results.title: 'Nazi vanity project': Eagle's Nest in Bavarian Alps a symbol of regime's 'conquest of nature'
results.content: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Sir Richard Evans, British Historian and Regius Professor Emeritus of History at the University of Cambridge. The controversy surrounding the fate of Adolf Hitler's Eagle's Nest, the Nazi-era mountaintop complex in the Bavarian Alps, raises profound questions about the relationship between architecture, historical memory and political extremism. At the heart of the debate lies a difficult distinction: preserving the material evidence of history is not necessarily the same as preserving the symbols through which a criminal regime sought to glorify itself. "This is a Nazi vanity project," Evans argues and his conclusion is unequivocal: the mountain must be "restored to its natural state."

results.title: 'We call it war-life balance': Daryna's daily struggle to live, survive in wartime Ukraine
results.content: Daryna, 25, entered adulthood in a country at war. Since Russia’s full-scale invasion, her days have been shaped by air raid alerts, power outages and nights spent sheltering in the subway. Despite the uncertainty that shadows every day, she is determined to preserve a semblance of normal life in Kyiv. FRANCE 24 met a young woman who has become emblematic of a generation learning to live under daily bombardment.

results.title: Trump says deportation crackdown was 'too tough' after midterm setback
results.content: US President Donald Trump said his administration's mass deportation campaign may have been "too tough" in a television interview aired Sunday, days after Republicans suffered heavy losses in midterm elections.

results.title: Poland braces for tense week after deadly Krakow shooting deepens political divisions
results.content: Poland faces a week of political tensions after its deadliest shooting in decades left six people dead and dozens wounded in Krakow on Saturday. The attack has heightened concerns over rising far-right extremism ahead of a major nationalist march.

results.title: Nvidia to probe reports that Chinese intelligence targeted CEO Jensen Huang
results.content: Nvidia’s board said Sunday it would investigate reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The New York Times reported Huang had an affair with an executive US intelligence believed was gathering information for Beijing. Huang will remain CEO during the inquiry and has pledged cooperation.
